c1: Eight months is the weak number. A new bakery often pays its owner nothing for a year or more. Start-up costs also land before the first sale: ovens, fit-out, permits, deposits, first stock. From savings, they shorten the eight months. From a loan, they add debt. The lease is the bigger risk. Commercial leases run for years. New tenants often have to sign a personal guarantee. That makes the rent your debt, not the bakery's. So the worst case isn't lost savings. It's years of rent on a closed shop. You can test the idea and keep the salary. Weekend markets and wholesale to cafés give you real sales at your prices. They also test the early starts and the volume.
c2: A mandate is evidence about executives, not about productivity. Executives also chose open-plan offices. The cleanest trial I know of ran at Trip.com. Two home days a week didn't lower performance. Quitting fell by a third. Fully remote is a different case, with real losses in several studies. And most of those orders are hybrid, not five days a week. That's close to the trial's setup.
c3: A growing square gains area along two edges, each x long. Take a square of side x and area x². Lengthen the side by a tiny amount h. The area gains two x-by-h strips and one small h-by-h corner. That's 2xh + h² of new area. Divide by h for the change per unit of side: 2x + h. Now let h shrink to zero. The lone h disappears, leaving 2x. This is the limit definition of the derivative, or differentiating from first principles.
c4: Months inside a book do that. Past a certain point you stop seeing the sentences. So not being able to tell isn't a verdict on the book. The standard fix is a few weeks away, then one straight read on paper. The dull stretches on that read are your real notes.
c5: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at one place and time. Climate is the statistics of that weather over a long stretch, usually thirty years. That means the averages, the spread and the frequency of extremes. Weather forecasts fade after about ten days. Climate can be projected decades ahead. One predicts a particular day. The other predicts the odds.
